plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: A herbaceous perennial producing large, fragrant, bowl-shaped double or single blooms atop sturdy stems with deeply lobed glossy green foliage. A beloved cottage garden staple that can live for decades.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June)
plants.location: Native to China and Siberia; widely cultivated in temperate gardens across North America and Europe
plants.funFact: Peonies can live and bloom for over 100 years, and ants visiting the buds are harmless and do not need to be removed for the flowers to open.

plants.name: Rosa gallica
plants.description: A deciduous shrub with fragrant, semi-double to double flowers and prickly stems. One of the oldest cultivated roses, it forms dense thickets and has been the parent of many garden varieties.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June)
plants.location: Central and southern Europe, and western Asia; cultivated worldwide in temperate gardens
plants.funFact: Dried petals of Rosa gallica 'Officinalis' keep their fragrance for years, which is why it was used by medieval apothecaries in Provins, France.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall tropical and subtropical tree with fern-like leaves that erupts in massive clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers, carpeting the ground beneath the canopy with purple petals.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Northern Hemisphere (May to June); September to November in parts of the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America; planted in Los Angeles, Mexico, South Africa, Australia and the Mediterranean
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, the thousands of jacaranda trees lining the streets earned it the nickname 'Jacaranda City'.

plants.name: Delphinium elatum
plants.description: A towering perennial with dense spikes of flowers up to 2 meters tall. Each spike is packed with individual blooms, often with a contrasting central 'bee' of petals.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to midsummer (May to July)
plants.location: Alpine meadows of Europe and Siberia; popular in temperate English-style gardens
plants.funFact: All parts of delphiniums are toxic to humans and livestock, yet their flower spikes are among the most prized in cut-flower arrangements.
